lesson_title: Filling and Wrapping: Prisms and Cylinders
hook_text: The formula 2πrh has been in your hands your whole life. Peel a can label.
clip_script: The can is the beautiful one. Peel the label off a real can: it comes away as a flat rectangle. Its height is the can's height, twelve. Its width is the distance the label travelled around the can — once around the circle, which is two pi times the radius, ten pi. So the label's area is ten pi times twelve, one hundred and twenty pi. Add the two circular ends, twenty-five pi each, and the total wrap is one hundred and seventy pi square centimetres.
visual_style: A cooldrink can spinning as its label peels off and flattens into a glowing rectangle, dimensions snapping into place, then the two lids floating in to complete the net.
pacing: Slow peel, then quick rhythmic assembly of the three net pieces.
